info.summary: Road hazard detection, validation, connected-vehicle collision prevention and community reporting.
info.description:
REST/JSON API of the **VIASafe Road Risk Analysis Platform** (CAMTRACK). It serves the web console,
the VIASafe mobile app, the vehicle simulator and approved integrations.

## Platform modules

| # | Module | Tags |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Security, users & roles | Authentication · Users · Roles & permissions · API clients |
| 2 | Dashboard | Dashboard & statistics |
| 3 | Maps, routes & geospatial | Map configuration · Routes & geocoding |
| 4 | Preliminary road-risk assessment (ARR) | *(web console — no dedicated endpoints yet)* |
| 5 | AI hazard detection | Detections · Datasets · AI models |
| 6 | Hazard track & human validation | Detections · Hazards · Cluster areas · Rejection reasons |
| 7 | Video/data ingestion & processing jobs | Jobs · Streams · Cloud connections |
| 8 | Historical risk analysis | Historical risk |
| 9 | Driver behaviour | *(uses Historical risk data)* |
| 10 | Connected vehicles & collision prevention | Vehicles & telemetry · Road state · Trajectory · Collisions · Alerts |
| 11 | Community reporting | Community reports |
| 12 | APIs & integration | API clients · Mobile configuration · this document |
| 13 | Configuration, audit & reporting | Platform settings · Audit trail · AI models |

## Authentication

Every operation lists the credentials it accepts (padlock icon) and, below its description, the
**Permission** it needs as `module:action` (actions: `view`, `add`, `edit`, `delete`; see
`GET /roles/modules`). A user's permissions are the union of their active roles.

### Users — session token (`BearerAuth`)

1. `POST /auth/login` with `{identifier, password, captcha_token}` (identifier = e-mail or username).
2. The answer's `status` is one of:
   * `ok` — `token` is an opaque session token valid until `expires_at`;
   * `mfa_required` — send the authenticator code with the returned `challenge_token` to
     `POST /auth/mfa/verify` (the challenge is valid a few minutes);
   * `mfa_setup_required` — the user's role requires MFA: call `POST /auth/mfa/setup` then
     `POST /auth/mfa/enable` with the `challenge_token`; enabling completes the sign-in.
3. Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every call. `POST /auth/logout`, a password change/reset or
   deactivation revokes the session immediately (`401 session_expired` afterwards).

Failed sign-ins count towards a lockout (`423 account_locked`, `locked_until` in the error).

### Mobile app & integrations — API key (`ApiKeyAuth`)

Keys are issued in *Administration → API clients* and sent as `X-API-Key: <key>`. A key only reaches
an explicit allow-list of endpoints (operations showing *API key* in their security); any other call
gets `403 forbidden`. The mobile app signs users in with `POST /auth/mobile/login`,
`POST /auth/mobile/register` or `POST /auth/google` and then sends **both** headers — the key never
gains the user's permissions; the user's token only identifies them (`/auth/me`, votes, reports).

### Development mode

When the server runs with `AUTH_ENFORCED=false` (demo stack) the permission checks of the module
routers are skipped and anonymous calls are accepted; user-administration endpoints still require a
signed-in user. API-key allow-lists always apply.

## Errors

Errors use HTTP status codes and a JSON body `{"detail": {"code": "<code>", "message": "<text>", …}}`
(model `ErrorResponse`). `code` is stable and meant for programs; `message` is for people; some errors
add fields (e.g. `module`/`action` on `forbidden`, `locked_until`, `requirements`, `errors`).
A few older endpoints still answer `{"detail": "<text>"}` (model `LegacyErrorResponse`), and request
validation errors use FastAPI's `{"detail": [{"loc", "msg", "type"}]}` (model `HTTPValidationError`).

| Status | Common codes |
|---|---|
| 400 | `captcha_failed`, `invalid_code`, `invalid_password`, `invalid_reset_token`, `mfa_not_started`, `google_not_configured`, `smtp_not_configured`, `cloud_not_configured`, `invalid_state`, `state_expired` |
| 401 | `not_authenticated`, `session_expired`, `invalid_api_key`, `api_key_required`, `invalid_credentials`, `challenge_expired`, `invalid_google_token` |
| 403 | `forbidden`, `account_inactive`, `mfa_required_by_role` |
| 404 | `not_found` |
| 409 | `invalid_transition`, `email_taken`, `username_taken`, `last_admin`, `role_in_use`, `system_role`, `signalement_inactive`, `not_authorized`, `connection_disabled` |
| 422 | `weak_password`, `invalid_sort`, `invalid_status`, `invalid_filter`, `invalid_reason`, `invalid_location`, `invalid_settings`, `unknown_role`, `device_id_required` |
| 423 | `account_locked` |
| 429 | `rate_limited` |
| 502 | `geocoding_failed`, `smtp_failed`, `google_failed`, `oauth_failed`, `cloud_failed` |
| 503 | `captcha_unavailable`, `google_unavailable`, `queue_unavailable` |

## Conventions

* **Pagination** — list endpoints take `skip` (offset, ≥ 0) and `limit` (page size; the maximum is
  given on each endpoint, typically 200, 500 for detection lists) and answer `{"total": n, "items": […]}`
  where `total` counts every match before paging.
* **Rate limits** — `POST /auth/mobile/register`: `MOBILE_REGISTER_PER_HOUR` attempts per client IP
  per hour (default 5) → `429 rate_limited`. Forgot-password requests send at most one e-mail per
  account per minute (the answer is identical either way). Geocoding is throttled upstream to one
  request per second (cached).
* **Time** — timestamps are ISO 8601 in **UTC**; naive values (no offset) are UTC.
* **Units** — distances and radii in **metres**, speeds in **m/s** (`speed_kmh` fields are km/h),
  accelerations in m/s², headings/bearings in degrees clockwise from north (0–360), durations in
  seconds unless the field name says otherwise.
* **Coordinates** — WGS84 decimal degrees, `latitude` ∈ [-90, 90], `longitude` ∈ [-180, 180].
* **Identifiers** — UUID strings unless stated otherwise.
* **Runtime settings** — distances and thresholds used by the endpoints (visibility radius, route
  corridor, vote distance, validation thresholds, collision levels …) come from *Platform settings*
  sections (`mobile`, `community`, `validation`, `collision`, `routes`, `security` …), editable at run time
  via `PUT /platform-settings/{section}` and published to the app by `GET /mobile-config/`.

## Interactive use

Click **Authorize**, paste a session token (from `POST /auth/login`) and/or an API key, then use
**Try it out**. Authorizations persist across page reloads in this browser. The same document is
served as JSON at `/openapi.json` and rendered by ReDoc at `/redoc`; a copy is committed in
`docs/openapi.json` (`python -m app.export_openapi`).

(RRAP-07-001). Answers `202 Accepted` with the job in status `pending`; follow it with

code) < `auto_reject` → `unknown_sign`, review; ≥ `auto_accept` → the classifier agrees) and

**Mobile — "Still there?" vote** (`present` / `absent`). Every vote is stored, but it is
**counted** only when the voter's position is within `community.vote_max_distance_m` metres of the

post.description:
**Mobile / simulator** — periodic position fix (every few seconds while driving). Units: WGS84
degrees, speed in **m/s**, heading in degrees clockwise from north, accuracy in metres,
acceleration in m/s²; out-of-range values (latitude/longitude, negative speed, acceleration
±20 m/s²) → 422. A speed above 100 m/s (360 km/h, e.g. the app's fast demo drive) is clamped to
100 m/s instead of being rejected. The fix becomes the vehicle's live state (expires after `VEHICLE_LIVE_TTL_S`
seconds without pings) and `last_seen` is updated (throttled).

After the 204 is sent, the collision pipeline runs in the background for this vehicle:
road-state map-matching → trajectory prediction → conflict assessment with nearby vehicles →
alert engine (may notify on a NEW / ESCALATED alert). Failures there never affect the ping.

AiValidationSettings.title: AiValidationSettings
AiValidationSettings.description:
AI validation mode (RRAP-05-012/016, RRAP-06-007, RRAP-13-001) — the
SINGLE source of the automatic decisions the video processor takes on new
detections (see app.modules.m05_ai_detection.ai_validation):

  manual     every detection goes to human review; the AI only suggests;
  assisted   auto-accept only when the detector AND (if required) the crop
             classifier are confident and the location is confirmed;
             auto-reject when the classifier (or a very low detector
             confidence) says no; everything else → review;
  automatic  decide whenever the classifier is confident either way.

Thresholds per type: `type_overrides` here, else the model cards
(app.modules.m05_ai_detection.model_registry), else section `validation`
(auto_accept_above / auto_reject_below), which remains the fallback when
no model card is installed. A random `audit_sample_rate` share of the
automatic decisions is left pending for a human (audit sample).

traffic_sign (two-stage: detector + sign-code classifier): the classifier
score is P(predicted code); thresholds per code (`type_overrides.traffic_sign
.per_class`, else the card's `thresholds.per_class`, else the type values).
P < auto_reject (or `unknown_sign` predicted) → subtype `unknown_sign`,
review; the card's reject class (`not_a_sign`) predicted confidently →
auto-reject `ai_not_a_sign`.

Video consistency: an auto-accept needs the object in ≥
`min_frames_for_auto_accept` sampled frames with an estimated position
drifting ≤ `max_static_drift_m` while the vehicle moves (else review,
`not_static`); a pothole box centre must lie below
`pothole_min_y_ratio` × frame height (else `off_road_area`, see below).

Pothole false-positive rules (app.modules.m05_ai_detection.static_check.pothole_rule_rejects),
on the best box of a finished track: box centre above the road-area line →
`pothole_off_road_action` `reject` (auto-reject `ai_off_road`) or `review`
(accept blocker `off_road_area` only); box wider than
`pothole_max_width_ratio` of the frame, larger than `pothole_max_area_ratio`
of it, or — with `pothole_reject_edge_touching` — touching the left/right
border (within 1 %) while wider than 25 % of the frame → auto-reject
`ai_box_too_large` (roadside earth, bushes, building edges). These
auto-rejects apply only in assisted / automatic mode; in manual mode they
are review hints (AI suggestion).

**Levels**: `SAFE` < `MONITOR` < `WARNING` < `HIGH_WARNING` < `CRITICAL`.
**Lifecycle** (`status`): `DETECTED` (first tick above SAFE) → `ACTIVE`
(ongoing, may escalate / de-escalate) → `RESOLVED` (terminal).
`transition` says what changed on the latest evaluation; consumers notify on
`NEW` / `ESCALATED`. De-escalation is delayed by a hysteresis
(`pending_level` / `pending_since`).

tags.name: Health
tags.description: **Module 0** — liveness probe for load balancers and monitoring.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description: **Module 1** — sign-in (password + CAPTCHA, mobile app, Google), multi-factor authentication (TOTP), sessions, the signed-in user's own profile and password reset. See the *Authentication* section of the introduction for the complete flow.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: **Module 1** — user administration (RRAP-01-010/011/012). Every change is audited. You cannot deactivate or delete yourself and the last active Administrator cannot be removed.

tags.name: Roles & permissions
tags.description: **Module 1** — roles and their View/Add/Edit/Delete matrix per permission module (RRAP-01-007/008/009/013). `GET /roles/modules` lists the module keys used in every `**Permission:** module:action` line of this documentation.

tags.name: API clients
tags.description: **Module 1 / 12** — API keys for the mobile app, the simulator and integrations (RRAP-12-015). The clear key is returned once, at creation or rotation; only its prefix is stored in clear.

tags.name: Dashboard & statistics
tags.description: **Module 2** — operational dashboard KPIs, time series and counters.

tags.name: Map configuration
tags.description: **Module 3** — base-map tiles the caller should display (OpenStreetMap or Google Map Tiles, per user preference — RRAP-01-012 / RRAP-03-001).

tags.name: Routes & geocoding
tags.description: **Module 3** — route-search helpers: predefined road sections (tronçons), OSRM driving route preview and Nominatim geocoding proxied by the server (cache, ≤ 1 upstream request/s).

tags.name: Detections
tags.description:
**Modules 5 & 6** — AI detections (potholes, traffic signs, speed bumps …) with their evidence, the human validation workflow and the spatial queries used by the mobile app.

**Review statuses** — `location_pending` (no confirmed position yet), `pending` (awaiting a decision), `validated` (accepted as predicted), `corrected` (accepted after a class or location correction), `rejected` (not a hazard — human or automatic rule), `resolved` (accepted hazard later fixed). Every transition writes a review-history row and an audit entry; anything outside this table is refused with `409 invalid_transition`:

| From | To | Actions |
|---|---|---|
| `location_pending` | `pending` | `location_fix` |
| `location_pending` | `rejected` | `auto_reject`, `reject` |
| `location_pending` | `validated` | `resight` |
| `pending` | `pending` | `location_fix` |
| `pending` | `validated` | `accept`, `auto_accept`, `resight` |
| `pending` | `corrected` | `accept`, `correct`, `resight` |
| `pending` | `rejected` | `auto_reject`, `reject` |
| `validated` | `resolved` | `resolve` |
| `corrected` | `resolved` | `resolve` |
| `resolved` | `validated` | `unresolve` |
| `resolved` | `corrected` | `unresolve` |
| `validated` | `pending` | `reopen` |
| `validated` | `location_pending` | `reopen` |
| `corrected` | `pending` | `reopen` |
| `corrected` | `location_pending` | `reopen` |
| `rejected` | `pending` | `reopen` |
| `rejected` | `location_pending` | `reopen` |
| `resolved` | `pending` | `reopen` |
| `resolved` | `location_pending` | `reopen` |

tags.name: Hazards
tags.description: **Module 6** — hazards: the de-duplicated physical road hazards that accepted detections are clustered into (status `active` → `resolved`, reopenable).

tags.name: Cluster configuration
tags.description: **Module 6** — the global Cluster Configuration (RRAP-06-009/010/011): one configuration with an **urban** (in agglomeration) and a **rural** (out of agglomeration) profile — default radius plus per-detection-type and per-report-type values — and **cluster zones** where it applies: agglomerations (city outlines from OpenStreetMap), road-section corridors along a tronçon (OSRM route) and custom polygons. Every detection (hazard clustering, processor de-duplication, re-sightings) and every community report (merging) is clustered with the radius resolved at its own position (`GET /cluster-zones/resolve`). `/cluster-config` and `/cluster-areas` are deprecated wrappers.

tags.name: Rejection reasons
tags.description: **Module 6** — catalogue of rejection reasons offered to validators, per detection type (`all` applies to every type). Seeded reasons cannot be removed.

tags.name: Datasets
tags.description: **Module 5** — training data for model improvement. *Live training data*: every decision on a detection (accept / correct incl. a moved box / reject, human or automatic; reopen removes it) keeps a training sample and writes, in the `datasets` bucket, the clean frame + YOLO label (`<type>/detector/`) and the padded crop (`<type>/classifier/<class>/`); list them with `GET /datasets/samples`, download with `GET /datasets/export`, write Label Studio box reviews back with `PUT /datasets/frames/…/labels` (docs/TRAINING-DATA.md). *Dataset versions*: immutable crop snapshots built from the validation labels (`POST /datasets/export`).

tags.name: AI models
tags.description: **Modules 5 & 13** — model registry and AI validation quality (RRAP-05-010/011/012/016, RRAP-13-016). Two-stage pothole pipeline: the detector proposes boxes, a crop classifier scores each crop (`verifier_score` = P(pothole)). Each weights file may come with a JSON *model card* (version, datasets, metrics, proposed thresholds). Settings section `ai_validation` picks the **mode** — `manual` (humans decide everything), `assisted` (default: automatic decision only when detector and classifier agree and the location is confirmed) or `automatic` (decide whenever the classifier is confident) — and the share of automatic decisions drawn for a human **audit**. Thresholds: `ai_validation.type_overrides`, else the model cards, else section `validation`. Automatic decisions are taken by actor `system` and reversible with `POST /detections/{id}/reopen`.

tags.name: Jobs
tags.description:
**Module 7** — video processing jobs (upload, cloud import, stream segment).

**Job statuses** — `pending` → `processing` → `done` | `failed` | `cancelled`. A `pending` or `processing` job can be cancelled; a `failed` or `cancelled` job can be retried while its source media is retained and `attempts < max_attempts`.

tags.name: Streams
tags.description: **Module 7** — RTSP/HTTP video streams recorded in segments and processed as jobs.

tags.name: Cloud connections
tags.description:
**Module 7 — input sources.** Google Drive / OneDrive accounts connected with OAuth: browse folders and files (`/browse`, `/thumbnail`), import a selection (`POST /{id}/imports`), and optionally auto-import a watched folder (`auto_import`). The OAuth *client* credentials stay in Platform settings → `cloud`.

**SFTP servers** (provider `sftp`) use the same browse / import endpoints (file and folder ids are absolute remote paths, confined to the server's base path). Create one with `POST /cloud-connections/sftp`; its `password` is write-only — stored encrypted, decrypted only to authenticate, never returned or logged (legacy servers may read `SFTP_PASSWORD_<KEY>` from `infra/secrets/sftp.env` instead). `…/sftp/connect`, `/disconnect`, `/forget-host-key` (host key trusted on first use) and `/log` (FileZilla-style connection log + live link state) complete it. See docs/SFTP-SOURCE.md.

tags.name: Cloud imports
tags.description:
**Module 7 — input sources.** Import batches created from a drive selection or a watched folder.

**Item statuses** — `queued` → `downloading` → `uploading_to_storage` → `queued_for_processing` → `processing` → `done`, or `failed` / `cancelled` / `skipped_duplicate`. Download progress (`bytes_done`, `percent`, `speed_bps`, `eta_s`) is live while downloading; afterwards the status and `job_progress` follow the processing job. Poll `GET /imports/{batch_id}` every 1–2 s while `active`.

tags.name: Historical risk
tags.description: **Module 8** (functional Module 4, Historical Risk Analysis) — historical driving events imported into stable grid cells and turned into normalised 0–1 risk scores: zone, route and heatmap queries, top risk zones, risk trend over time, import history.

tags.name: Driver behaviour
tags.description: **Module 9** (functional Module 5, Driver Behaviour Analytics, RRAP-09) — speeding, harsh braking, hard acceleration and harsh cornering events (stored in the historical event store): KPIs per behaviour, driver / vehicle risk scores and rankings, heatmaps, time trends and high-risk behaviour zones. Scores are event-based indicators, not accident probabilities.

tags.name: Vehicles & telemetry
tags.description: **Module 10** — vehicle/device registration and live telemetry pings (WGS84, m/s). A ping feeds the road-state → trajectory → collision → alert pipeline.

tags.name: Road state
tags.description: **Module 10** — map-matched road context of a live vehicle (segment, lane direction, road class …).

tags.name: Trajectory
tags.description: **Module 10** — short-horizon trajectory prediction of a live vehicle along the road network.

tags.name: Collisions
tags.description: **Module 10** — pairwise conflict analysis between live vehicles (distance, time-to-collision, risk level).

tags.name: Alerts
tags.description: **Module 10** — driver alerts derived from conflicts. **Levels**: `SAFE` < `MONITOR` < `WARNING` < `HIGH_WARNING` < `CRITICAL`; **lifecycle**: `DETECTED` → `ACTIVE` → `RESOLVED`.

tags.name: Community reports
tags.description: **Module 11** — community reports (*signalements*) from the mobile app and their community validation: present/absent votes counted only within `community.vote_max_distance_m`, one per voter; passes (driving by without voting) mark a report *uncertain*. **Statuses**: `actif`, `annule`, `rejete` (moderation). **Vote outcomes** (`reason`): `too_far`, `duplicate`, `no_position`.

tags.name: Mobile configuration
tags.description: **Module 12** — runtime distances and thresholds the mobile app works with (Settings → Mobile app distances / Community reporting / Collision prevention).

tags.name: Platform settings
tags.description: **Module 13** — platform settings by section (CAPTCHA, SMTP, maps, security policy, validation rules, AI validation mode, mobile, community, collision …). Secrets are write-only; changes are audited.

tags.name: Audit trail
tags.description: **Module 13** — audit trail of sign-ins, administrative changes and every state-changing user call (RRAP-13-006).

tags.name: Reports
tags.description: **Module 14** — PDF reports generated server-side (AI hazards, community reports, historical risk, driver behaviour, collision prevention) with type, period, area and path (road section or from → to corridor) filters; generated files are kept for re-download (RRAP-13-011/012/013).
